meta_description: Cost per resolved task — not per token — is the real unit of GenAI economics.

blocks.x: Cost per resolved task — not per token — is the real unit of GenAI economics.
GenAI unit economics: the metric nobody tracks. Routing across model tiers cuts cost 40-60% at equal task quality on most workloads.
Distillation to right-sized models converts frontier quality into commodity cost.
Caching and prompt discipline matter more than model choice for high-volume flows.

Applied carelessly, it breaks the same way every time — retrieval appended after the model choice, permissions mapped after launch, freshness treated as an ops afterthought — each producing the same symptom: answers nobody defends when the audit arrives.
The serious opposition goes: the retrieval-first thesis can excuse weak models. It should not: retrieval multiplies whatever the model does, so evaluation stays the arbiter in both directions.
How we put it to work

In delivery, this thesis becomes a specific discipline: the work is model and retrieval engineering with evaluation wired in from the first sprint — grounded answers, cited sources, and a cost line somebody actually owns. Every program in the Applied AI & GenAI domain carries the same obligations — a signed baseline, named gate criteria, and evidence generated by running the system rather than preparing for a meeting.
Talk to the team that runs genAI unit economics: the metric nobody tracks in production — the briefing is technical by design, and the first one costs nothing but the hour.
